title: ✈️ How Is International Shipping Fee Calculated?
content:
International shipping fees are usually calculated after your items arrive at our China warehouse. The final fee depends on the actual package weight, package size, destination country, shipping method, and product type.

This guide explains the main factors that affect your shipping fee.


🌟 Simple overview

International shipping fee is usually calculated based on:

  1. Destination country or region
  2. Shipping method
  3. Actual weight
  4. Package size
  5. Chargeable weight
  6. Product type
  7. Extra warehouse services
  8. Customs or tax handling rules, if applicable

Different shipping methods may use different calculation rules. Please always check the final amount shown on the parcel submission page.


1. 🌍 Destination country or region

The destination country is one of the most important factors.

Shipping to different countries may have different prices because of:

  • Flight cost
  • Distance
  • Local delivery cost
  • Customs handling
  • Fuel surcharge
  • Remote area surcharge
  • Local courier fees

For example, shipping the same package to the United States, Japan, Canada, Europe, or Australia may result in different shipping fees.

Even within the same country, some remote areas may cost more.


2. 🚚 Shipping method

Different shipping methods have different prices and delivery times.

Common shipping method differences include:

  • Economy shipping: usually cheaper, but slower
  • Standard shipping: balanced price and delivery time
  • Express shipping: usually faster, but more expensive
  • Tax-included shipping: may include some customs or tax handling
  • Sensitive item shipping: supports special items, but may cost more
  • Sea shipping: suitable for heavy or large items, but slower
  • Air shipping: faster, but usually more expensive than sea shipping

When choosing a shipping method, please do not only compare the price. You should also check the delivery time, item restrictions, tracking details, and compensation rules.


3. ⚖️ Actual weight

Actual weight is the real weight of the parcel measured by our warehouse.

After your items arrive at our warehouse, the warehouse may weigh the item or final package.

For example:

  • Item weight: 1.2 kg
  • Packaging weight: 0.3 kg
  • Final actual weight: 1.5 kg

In this case, the actual weight used for shipping calculation may be 1.5 kg.

Please note that packaging materials may increase the final weight.


4. 📏 Package size

Package size means the length, width, and height of the parcel after packing.

Some items are not heavy, but they are large. These items may take up more space during international transportation.

Examples include:

  • Shoes with shoe boxes
  • Plush toys
  • Storage boxes
  • Lamps
  • Hats
  • Bags with large packaging
  • Home decoration items
  • Large but lightweight products

For these products, the shipping fee may be affected by volume weight.


5. 📦 Volume weight

Volume weight is calculated based on package size.

Some logistics companies compare the actual weight and the volume weight, then use the larger one as the chargeable weight.

This is because a large package takes up more space, even if it is not very heavy.

A common volume weight formula is:

Length × Width × Height ÷ Volume divisor

The volume divisor may be different for different shipping methods.

For example:

  • Some routes may use 5000
  • Some routes may use 6000
  • Some routes may use other calculation rules

Please check the shipping method details for the exact rule.


6. 🧾 Chargeable weight

Chargeable weight is the weight used to calculate your shipping fee.

In many cases, the logistics company will compare:

  • Actual weight
  • Volume weight

Then it will use the higher one as the chargeable weight.

Example:

  • Actual weight: 3 kg
  • Volume weight: 5 kg
  • Chargeable weight: 5 kg

In this case, the shipping fee may be calculated based on 5 kg.

This is why a large but lightweight item may sometimes cost more to ship than expected.


7. 🪜 First weight and additional weight

Some shipping methods use a “first weight + additional weight” pricing rule.

For example:

  • First weight: 0.5 kg
  • Additional weight: 0.5 kg

If your parcel weighs 1.2 kg, the logistics company may charge it as 1.5 kg.

This is because the parcel weight is rounded up based on the route’s billing unit.

Different shipping methods may have different billing units, such as:

  • 0.1 kg
  • 0.5 kg
  • 1 kg

Please check the shipping method details before submitting your parcel.


8. 🔋 Product type

The product type may also affect the available shipping methods and shipping fee.

Some products are considered restricted or sensitive items.

Examples include:

  • Battery products
  • Electronic products
  • Liquid products
  • Powder products
  • Cosmetics
  • Food
  • Medicine or supplements
  • Magnetic items
  • Branded goods
  • Fragile items
  • Oversized items

These products may not be accepted by all shipping methods.

If a product requires a special shipping route, the shipping fee may be higher than normal products.


9. 🛠️ Extra warehouse services

Some optional warehouse services may affect the final shipping fee.

For example:

Reinforcement

Reinforcement can help protect fragile or valuable items, but it may increase the package weight and size.

Removing packaging

Removing unnecessary outer packaging may reduce the package size in some cases.

Keeping original boxes

Keeping shoe boxes, gift boxes, or large original packaging may increase volume weight.

Waterproof packaging

Waterproof packaging may add a small amount of weight, but it can improve parcel protection.

Before choosing extra services, please consider both item protection and shipping cost.


10. 📦 Consolidation

Consolidation means combining multiple warehouse items into one international parcel.

This may help reduce shipping cost in some cases because you can avoid paying the first weight fee multiple times.

For example:

  • Shipping 3 items separately may require 3 separate parcels
  • Combining them may create 1 parcel with one shipping fee

However, consolidation does not always guarantee a lower fee.

If the combined parcel becomes too large, the volume weight may increase.

The final cost depends on the actual package weight, size, and selected shipping method.


11. 🧮 Why is the estimated shipping fee different from the final fee?

The estimated shipping fee is only for reference.

The final fee may be different because:

  • The actual item weight is different from the estimated weight
  • The seller’s packaging is larger than expected
  • The final parcel size is larger after packing
  • You selected reinforcement or extra packaging
  • The logistics company charges by volume weight
  • You changed the shipping method
  • You combined multiple items
  • The destination country or route price changed
  • The item requires a special shipping method

The final shipping fee is based on the actual parcel information after warehouse processing.


12. 💡 How to reduce international shipping cost

Here are some tips that may help reduce your shipping cost:

  • Combine multiple items when suitable
  • Remove unnecessary packaging if you do not need it
  • Avoid buying very large but lightweight items
  • Choose economy shipping if delivery time is not urgent
  • Use sea shipping for large or heavy goods, if available
  • Check the estimated shipping fee before buying oversized products
  • Avoid restricted items unless necessary
  • Submit your parcel before the free storage period ends
  • Contact customer service before buying large, fragile, or special items

Please note: the cheapest shipping method may not always be the best choice. For valuable, fragile, or urgent items, a safer or faster method may be more suitable.


Example 1: Small clothing parcel

You buy several T-shirts.

The package is small and lightweight.

In this case, the shipping fee may be mainly based on actual weight.

This type of parcel is usually easier to ship and may have more available shipping methods.


Example 2: Shoes with shoe box

You buy one pair of shoes and choose to keep the shoe box.

The actual weight may not be very high, but the shoe box increases the package size.

In this case, the shipping fee may be affected by volume weight.

If you do not need the shoe box, you may request to remove it before shipping.


Example 3: Large plush toy

You buy a large plush toy.

The item may be lightweight, but the package size is large.

The logistics company may charge based on volume weight instead of actual weight.

This is why large plush toys may have higher international shipping fees.


Important notes

  • International shipping is usually calculated after items arrive at our warehouse.
  • Final shipping fee depends on actual weight, package size, destination, and shipping method.
  • Some shipping methods use volume weight.
  • Large but lightweight items may cost more than expected.
  • Consolidation may reduce cost in some cases, but not always.
  • Extra packaging may protect items but may also increase shipping cost.
  • The estimated shipping fee is for reference only.
  • The final fee shown before payment is the amount you need to pay for shipping.


Frequently Asked Questions

Q1: Why is my shipping fee higher than I expected?

Possible reasons include package size, volume weight, selected shipping method, destination country, product type, or extra packaging. Large but lightweight items often cost more because they take up more space.

Q2: What is chargeable weight?

Chargeable weight is the weight used to calculate the shipping fee. It may be based on actual weight or volume weight, depending on which one is higher.

Q3: Can I reduce the shipping fee by removing packaging?

Sometimes yes. Removing unnecessary packaging may reduce the package size. However, for fragile or valuable items, keeping protective packaging may be safer.

Q4: Is consolidation always cheaper?

Not always. Consolidation may help reduce repeated first weight charges, but if the final parcel becomes too large, volume weight may increase.

Q5: Why can’t the final shipping fee be calculated before purchase?

Because we do not know the actual item weight, package size, seller packaging, and final shipping method before the item arrives at our warehouse.

Q6: Which shipping method should I choose?

It depends on your destination country, item type, budget, and delivery time requirement. If you are not sure, please contact customer service before submitting the parcel.


Need help?

If you are unsure about the shipping fee, please contact our customer service team before submitting your parcel.

To help us assist you faster, please provide:

  • Destination country
  • Product link or screenshot
  • Item quantity
  • Estimated item weight, if available
  • Whether you want to keep or remove packaging
  • Your preferred delivery time
  • Your parcel number, if available

We will help you understand the available shipping methods and estimated cost.
